title: Algorithms
tagline: Correctness and recurrences, divide and conquer, sorting and selection, graph algorithms, greedy algorithms, dynamic programming, network flow and randomised algorithms
summary: An algorithm is a precise method for solving a problem, and its analysis tells us how its cost grows with the size of the input. This course teaches the main design techniques — divide and conquer, greedy choice, dynamic programming and reduction to network flow — together with proofs of correctness, the analysis of running time, graph algorithms and randomised algorithms.

chapters.title: Correctness and recurrences
chapters.summary: Loop invariants and induction for correctness, and solving recurrences with recursion trees and the master theorem.

chapters.title: Divide and conquer
chapters.summary: Mergesort, quicksort, fast integer multiplication and the closest pair of points, with their analyses.

chapters.title: Sorting lower bounds and selection
chapters.summary: The comparison lower bound for sorting, counting and radix sort, and linear-time selection.

chapters.title: Graph search and its applications
chapters.summary: Breadth- and depth-first search, topological sorting, strongly connected components and bipartite graphs.

chapters.title: Shortest paths
chapters.summary: Dijkstra’s algorithm, Bellman–Ford and negative cycles, and all-pairs shortest paths.

chapters.title: Greedy algorithms and spanning trees
chapters.summary: Exchange arguments, interval scheduling, Huffman codes, and Kruskal’s and Prim’s algorithms with union–find.

chapters.title: Dynamic programming
chapters.summary: Optimal substructure, memoisation and tabulation, with sequence alignment, knapsack and shortest paths.

chapters.title: Network flow and matching
chapters.summary: The Ford–Fulkerson method, the max-flow min-cut theorem, and bipartite matching by reduction to flow.

chapters.title: Randomised algorithms
chapters.summary: Las Vegas and Monte Carlo algorithms, expected running time, universal hashing and randomised minimum cut.
